Title: Admins are unable to access the Exchange admin center (EAC)

User impact: Admins are unable to access the EAC. 

More info: When attempting to access the Exchange admin center, admins encounter an “Internal Server Error” message.
 
Current status: Our testing has identified a recent Exchange admin center (EAC) configuration change as a potential contributor to the access failures and associated HTTP 302 redirects. We’re rolling back the change, which we expect to complete within approximately two hours. Once complete, we’ll monitor the environment to determine whether this resolves the impact.
 
Scope of impact: Impact may be specific to any admin attempting to access the EAC. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.

Next update by: Monday, October 12, 2026, at 1:30 PM UTC

We’re continuing to roll back the identified Exchange admin center (EAC) change. Initial telemetry shows errors trending downward from their earlier peak, and we’re monitoring service health to determine whether the rollback restores access for affected admins.
 
This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue.
 
Next update by: Monday, October 12, 2026, at 1:30 PM UTC

We’ve completed the rollback and are continuing to monitor service health, with telemetry showing errors trending downward from their earlier peak. Admins who continue to experience impact should close their existing Exchange admin center (EAC) browser session, open a new session, and retry accessing the EAC. We’ll continue monitoring to validate recovery.

Title: Admins are unable to access the Exchange admin center (EAC)

User impact: Admins are unable to access the EAC. 

More info: When attempting to access the Exchange admin center, affected admins encountered an “Internal Server Error” message.
 
Final status: We've completed the rollback of the identified Exchange admin center (EAC) change. Service telemetry shows that errors have returned to expected levels, and user reports have confirmed that EAC access has been restored. Admins who continue to experience impact should close their existing EAC browser session, open a new session, and retry accessing the EAC. We’ll continue to monitor service health to ensure sustained service stability.
 
Scope of impact: Impact was specific to admins attempting to access the EAC.
 
Start time: Monday, October 12, 2026, at 8:15 AM UTC
 
End time: Monday, October 12, 2026, at 12:50 PM UTC
 
Preliminary root cause: A recent EAC configuration change resulted in unexpected HTTP responses within the affected request path, preventing admins from successfully accessing the EAC. Reverting the identified change restored expected service functionality.
 
Next steps:
- We’re reviewing the identified EAC change and associated service configuration to help prevent similar impact from recurring.
- We’re reviewing our monitoring and telemetry to improve detection and alerting for similar service behavior.
 
We’ll provide a preliminary Post-Incident Report within two business days and a final Post-Incident Report within five business days.
